name: Gregory Garrabrants
current_role: President and CEO, Axos Financial, Inc. (NYSE: AX) and Axos Bank
profile: Greg Garrabrants has run Axos Financial (formerly BofI Holding / Bank of Internet USA) since October 2007, turning a small online thrift into a diversified, digital-first bank and financial services group with consumer and commercial banking, brokerage and advisory arms. His wealth comes from his Axos equity.
interesting_fact: Axos says that under his leadership total bank assets grew to about $24.8 billion and market value rose more than 30-fold; he describes it as: 'We didn't transform traditional banking. We created something new, built for the future.'
deep_cut_fact: Before banking he trained as an engineer and lawyer: a USC industrial and systems engineering graduate with a Northwestern JD and Kellogg MBA, he clerked for a federal judge and is a CFA charterholder and member of the California Bar, with stints at Deloitte, Goldman Sachs and McKinsey.

public_contacts.value: jlai@axosfinancial.com (Johnny Lai, SVP Corporate Development & IR; also listed as media contact)

notes: Axos's exec bio links to his LinkedIn. Company press/IR route goes through Johnny Lai (some 2026 releases list jlai@axosbank.com instead). Gives regular CEO interviews to The Wall Street Transcript.

name: Timothy Price Crain II
current_role: Co-founder; SVP & Chief Technology Officer (also styled Chief Growth Officer in 2025 releases), Intuitive Machines (Nasdaq: LUNR)
profile: Tim Crain is a former NASA Johnson Space Center engineer who in 2013 co-founded Houston's Intuitive Machines with Steve Altemus and Kam Ghaffarian, initially as a think tank applying human-spaceflight engineering to other fields. The firm pivoted to lunar landers under NASA's CLPS program; his wealth comes from his LUNR stake.
interesting_fact: Intuitive Machines' Odysseus (IM-1) became the first commercial spacecraft to land softly on the Moon in Feb 2024. Crain on the pivot: 'We dipped our toe in the let's-develop-the-moon river and promptly got pulled all the way in.'
deep_cut_fact: A UT Austin aerospace PhD and NSF graduate fellow (1996-2000), he was flight dynamics lead on NASA's low-cost Project Morpheus lander from 2009, and holds a NASA Space Act Award, two Exceptional Achievement Medals and the Outstanding Young Texas Ex award.

public_contacts.value: Previously a guest on Houston Innovators Podcast (ep. 208)

notes: Frequent conference speaker (Space Symposium, AIAA) and podcast guest; also leads IM's space nuclear power work, which suits the energy angle. Exact current title varies (CTO vs Chief Growth Officer).

name: Matthew J Wallach
current_role: Co-founder and board director, Veeva Systems (NYSE: VEEV); board member, HealthVerity
profile: Matt Wallach co-founded Veeva Systems in 2007 with Peter Gassner and served as president (strategy, alliances, business development) through the 2013 IPO until retiring in 2019. Veeva became the dominant cloud software provider for life sciences; he now sits on Veeva's and HealthVerity's boards and advises emerging tech companies.
interesting_fact: Veeva was one of the first large companies to convert to a public benefit corporation (2021). Before Veeva, Wallach was CMO of healthcare data firm Health Market Science and started at Booz & Company consulting to chemicals and pharma.
deep_cut_fact: A lifelong soccer player who grew up near Philadelphia: he played travel/ODP and Division I soccer at Yale (Ivy League champions in his sophomore year), has coached youth teams and still plays in a men's over-35 league.
notes: Retired from operating role; has a bio on the Philadelphia Union club site (soccer link is a natural opener). Reaching him via Veeva PR is indirect; HealthVerity board is another affiliation.

name: AD Padmasingh Isaac
current_role: Founder and Chairman/Managing Director, Aachi Group (Aachi Masala Foods Pvt Ltd), Chennai
profile: A first-generation entrepreneur from Nazareth in Tirunelveli district, Tamil Nadu, Padmasingh Isaac worked in sales at Godrej in the early 1980s before founding Aachi Masala in 1995-96. Selling Rs 2 sachets of ready curry masala to rural and working households, he built Aachi into a South Indian spice and packaged-food group reported at Rs 1,000+ crore revenue with about 3,500 staff.
interesting_fact: Aachi was rated 'Asia's Fastest Growing FMCG Brand' (2014) and 'India's No 1 Most Trusted Brand 2015' (Trust Research Advisory); he won TiECon Chennai's 'Extreme Entrepreneur of the Year 2010'.
deep_cut_fact: He is a published author: his book 'Enjoy Success, Relish Failures' (Rupa Publications) draws on his early struggles, and he holds advisory roles at the Indian Institute of Crop Processing Technology, Thanjavur, and NIFTEM in Haryana.
notes: Alive status assumed (no death reports found), but no 2024-26 news coverage turned up. Only a general company/customer-care email is published; no press office. He is a motivational speaker at youth forums, so speaking invitations or his publisher (Rupa) could be routes in. Hurun data is old (2018-19).
